title: Fundraisers
description: Organize activities to raise funds or otherwise solicit and gather monetary donations or other gifts for an organization. May design and produce promotional materials. May also raise awareness of the organization's work, goals, and financial needs.

tasks.text: Monitor progress of fundraising drives.
Monitor budgets, expense reports, or other financial data for fundraising organizations.
Develop strategies to encourage new or increased contributions.
Develop or implement fundraising activities, such as annual giving campaigns or direct mail programs.
Conduct research to identify the goals, net worth, charitable donation history, or other data related to potential donors, potential investors, or general donor markets.
Develop fundraising activity plans that maximize participation or contributions and minimize costs.
Establish fundraising or participation goals for special events or specified time periods.
Design or produce materials such as posters, Web sites, or newsletters to promote, market, or advertise fundraising events.
Write speeches, press releases, or other promotional materials to increase awareness of the causes, missions, or goals of organizations seeking funds.
Develop corporate fundraising programs, such as employer gift-matching.
Create or update donor databases.
Compile or develop materials to submit to granting or other funding organizations.
Write reports or prepare presentations to communicate fundraising program data.
Prepare materials such as fundraising envelopes, bid sheets, or gift bags for charitable events.
Identify and build relationships with potential donors.
Secure commitments of participation or donation from individuals or corporate donors.
Write and send letters of thanks to donors.
Solicit cash or in-kind donations or sponsorships from individual, business, or government donors.
Direct or supervise fundraising staff, including volunteer staff members.
Recruit sponsors, participants, or volunteers for fundraising events.
Contact corporate representatives, government officials, or community leaders to increase awareness of organizational causes, activities, or needs.
Attend community events, meetings, or conferences to promote organizational goals or solicit donations or sponsorships.
Explain the tax advantages of contributions to potential donors.
Plan and direct special events for fundraising, such as silent auctions, dances, golf events, or walks.
Coordinate transportation or delivery of materials, supplies, or donations for fundraising events.
Direct or coordinate Web-based fundraising activities, such as online auctions or donation Web sites.
Secure speakers for charitable events, community meetings, or conferences to increase awareness of charitable, nonprofit, or political causes.
Develop and maintain media contact lists.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Management of Financial Resources
skills.def: Determining how money will be spent to get the work done, and accounting for these expenditures.

skills.name: Customer relationship management CRM software
skills.def: Software to manage customer interactions. Examples: AudienceView Ticketing, Blackbaud eTapestry, Blackbaud Luminate CRM, Blackbaud The Raiser's Edge.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.
